result_text:
The Duplication report now has a "Most Frequent Duplicates" section right after "Longest Duplicates", and its code fragments are saved when `saveCodeFragments` is on. The compile succeeds and the related tests pass (`DuplicationAnalyzerTest`, `DuplicationEngineTest`, `DuplicationInstanceTest`, `DuplicateFileBlockExportInfoTest`). I did not render a report to check the HTML by eye.

The changes, all in the `repo` checkout, nothing committed:

- **`reports/.../generators/statichtml/DuplicationReportGenerator.java`**: `addMostFrequentDuplicatesList` already existed but was never called. I call it from `addDuplicationToReport` right after the longest-duplicates section. It was already written to skip the section when the list is empty and to use the description "The list of N most frequently found duplicates."
- **`reports/.../dataexporters/DataExporter.java`**:
  - Fragments are saved as `most_frequent_duplicates/most_frequent_duplicates_<n>.<ext>`, next to the longest duplicates and unit duplicates.
  - The source files of the most frequent duplicates are added to the referenced files, the same way longest duplicates already are, so they are cached when source caching is on.
- **`codeanalyzer/.../analysis/files/DuplicationAnalyzer.java`**: this is a fix beyond the request. `addMostFrequentDuplicates` sorted a throwaway copy (`Collections.sort(new ArrayList<>(duplicates), …)`), so the "most frequent" list was just the first N duplicates in arbitrary order. It now sorts a copy and takes the top N from that. This changes which duplicates are stored and exported, so it's worth a look if you want that separate.
